title: Feature Inventory
description: Traceable scope extracted from project source documents. Consumed by est-estimate. Every feature cites the source text that produced it; every part of the source not treated as scope is accounted for in not_scope.

granularity.description: What this inventory covers. Drives which fidelity mode est-estimate defaults to.

sources.description: One entry per source document ingested. Populated from the convert-input manifest.

language.description: BCP-47 code of the source's own language, e.g. en, uk, de

converter.description: Which converter produced the normalized text

coverage_note.description: Anything the converter could not read: scanned pages, images, password-protected sections

citations.description: At least one. A feature with no citation is invented scope.

location.description: Section heading, page, sheet+row, or transcript timestamp

quote.description: Verbatim source text, translated into the working language when the source is not in it

quote_original.description: Required when the source language differs from the working language. The untranslated text, so a reader who speaks the source language can verify the extraction.

scope_status.description: Whether the feature falls inside the contractually agreed scope. Absent means in_agreed_scope. Set outside_agreed_scope for a feature a source raises but the SOW or RFP does not cover — it is still estimated, and est-estimate reports it as a separate line rather than folding it into the agreed number.

commitment.description: committed: the source states it as in scope. implied: follows necessarily from something committed. speculative: raised as a possibility, a future phase, or a client aspiration.

evidence.description: The source text stating the dependency. Omit when inferred is true.

inferred.description: true when the dependency is deduced rather than stated. Inferred dependencies need human confirmation.

open_questions.description: What the source failed to say about this feature. Feeds est-estimate's range-narrowing question list.

epic_id.description: The epic this story belongs to. Planning is priced per epic, so this is what stops the estimate inventing an epic count from a ratio when the source already grouped the work.

surfaces.description: Which kinds of work this story touches. It decides which roles are billed to it: a role whose surface is absent is dropped from the split entirely, which is what keeps BA and UX hours off a pure backend task. Omitting it is not a way to say 'none' — an untagged story keeps every role, because silence must not quietly discount. Extraction states which kinds of work a story touches; est-estimate decides what it costs. This is the one classification-shaped field that stays here, because it is an observation about the scope rather than a judgement about effort.

tasks.description: The source rows this story was assembled from. A spreadsheet line is an acceptance criterion, not an estimable unit; pricing one per row multiplied a backlog into a project. The rows still have to be here, because a reviewer verifies the inventory against the client's own document line by line, and that is only possible if every line still appears.

location.description: Section heading, page, sheet+row, or transcript timestamp

quote.description: Verbatim source text, translated into the working language when the source is not in it

quote_original.description: Required when the source language differs from the working language. The untranslated text, so a reader who speaks the source language can verify the extraction.

features.description: The estimable units — stories, not source rows. Each carries the source rows it was assembled from as `tasks`.

not_scope.description: Source content that did NOT become a feature, with the reason. Empty only when every substantive passage produced a feature.

reason.description: Why it is not scope: commercial terms, background, out-of-scope statement, duplicate of Fnn, already built, unintelligible

conflicts.description: Sources that disagree. Surfaced, never silently resolved.

assumptions.description: What had to be assumed to produce this inventory. Carried into the estimate's assumptions block.

completeness_signals.description: Model-set signals about what the sources do and do not say. inventory-check.py turns these into the input completeness score under fixed published weights, and that score determines estimate band width in est-estimate. The weights are not negotiable per run; the signals are judgement, so each carries a 'why' held to the same standard as a feature tag's.

epics.description: Groups of stories, taken from the source wherever the source has them — a spreadsheet's epic column, a PRD's sections, an existing backlog's structure. Synthesised only where it does not, and then marked as such.

origin.description: source: the document grouped it. synthesised: extraction grouped it, and the why says on what basis.

citations.description: At least one. A feature with no citation is invented scope.

location.description: Section heading, page, sheet+row, or transcript timestamp

quote.description: Verbatim source text, translated into the working language when the source is not in it

quote_original.description: Required when the source language differs from the working language. The untranslated text, so a reader who speaks the source language can verify the extraction.

implicit_scope.description: Work this project will certainly do that the client's document never describes — a data migration implied by 'we have ten years of bookings', a reporting backfill, an integration environment. Priced exactly like a feature and shown in the same table, but held apart in the schema so that the two-way traceability guarantee over `features` stays absolute rather than being loosened for everything to accommodate a few entries. Work that EVERY project does — repo scaffold, pipeline, environments, release process — is not here: it comes from the cost model's `standing_work` catalogue, so it is the same on every estimate.

id.description: Its own prefix, so implicit scope can never be mistaken for an extracted feature in a diff, a ledger entry or a client-facing table.

rationale.description: Why this work is certain to happen although no passage asks for it — the sentence in the source that implies it, or the delivery fact that makes it unavoidable. This replaces the citation, and it is required for exactly that reason: work with neither a quote nor a reason is invented scope.

why.description: One line, citing what in the sources decided it. A signal without a reason is the same black box as a tag without one — and it carries more weight, since it sets the width of the whole estimate.
